reproduced.user_belief_vs_reality: a user who learned from the console script that --token auto is safe (it refuses a remote bind and prints a strong loopback token) believes typing it again gets the same safety; they get a real LAN listener whose entire secret is the four characters 'auto' -- not anonymous (anon is 401), which is exactly why it is a trap rather than an obvious hole.

rule: --token auto never means the literal secret 'auto': on loopback it generates a strong random token and prints it, and on a non-loopback bind it is refused (exit 2, nothing bound) because the token there gates every route and must be operator-chosen -- the same rule resextract serve already used.
